purpose: Baloxavir marboxil is used to treat influenza, commonly known as the flu, in people who have had symptoms for no more than 48 hours. It can also be used to help prevent the flu after you have been exposed to someone who has it. It works best when started as soon as possible after symptoms begin.
how_it_works: The flu virus needs a special tool called cap-dependent endonuclease to make copies of itself inside your body. Baloxavir blocks that tool, so the virus cannot reproduce and spread. This helps your immune system fight off the infection faster and shortens how long you feel sick.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, bronchitis, nausea, headache, and runny nose. Most people tolerate this medication well since it is usually just a single dose.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or trying to become pregnant, as safety in these situations is not fully established. Avoid taking it with dairy products, calcium-rich foods, or antacids containing calcium, magnesium, or aluminum right around the time of your dose, as these can reduce how well the medicine works. It is not a substitute for the annual flu vaccine, so make sure you still get vaccinated each year.
typical_dosing: For most adults and children 40 kg (about 88 lbs) or more, the dose is a single 80 mg tablet taken by mouth one time. Children between 20-40 kg typically take a single 40 mg dose. Because it is usually just one dose, it is very convenient — no need to remember multiple days of medication.
